1.title: Automated Investigation, Response and Automatic Attack Disruption
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Automated Investigation, Response and Automatic Attack Disruption. It covers the exam area one. Manage a security operations environment. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Manage automated investigation and response capabilities in Microsoft Defender X D R. Configure automatic attack disruption in Microsoft Defender X D R. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one. Manage a security operations environment (forty to forty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Automated investigation and response (AIR)
1.text: Automated investigation and response (A I R). The figure shows this: A I R investigates, then the automation level decides whether a person approves the actions.

1.title: Automated investigation and response (AIR), continued
1.text: Automated investigation and response (A I R). A I R examines an alert, collects evidence, gives each piece of evidence a verdict and proposes or takes remediation actions. Covers. Devices (Defender for Endpoint), on-premises A D users (Defender for Identity), email (Defender for Office three sixty-five). Verdicts. Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found. Approval. Actions that need approval wait in Action center, then Pending. Approve with. Security Administrator, or the unified R back permission Security operations Security data Response (manage). Bulk approval. Multi-select works for actions of the same type. Level that controls it. The automation level of the device group (Module three).

1.title: Automated investigation and response (AIR), continued
1.text: Automated investigation and response (A I R). Documented change: since September one, twenty twenty-six, A I R no longer runs as a separate investigation experience or manual trigger for Defender for Endpoint alerts. A I R for Defender for Office three sixty-five remains. Learn the Action center workflow; it is the same place where all response actions are approved. Exam tip: Pending equals waiting for a person. Full automation equals no approval. Approvals live in the Action center, with Pending and History tabs.

1.title: The Action center
1.text: The Action center. Pending. Approve or reject actions; select several of the same type. History. Audit log of completed actions; undo is possible for some. Action sources include manual device action, manual email action, automated device action, automated email action, advanced hunting action, Explorer action and live response action. Path: Actions and submissions, then Action center.

1.title: Automatic attack disruption
1.text: Automatic attack disruption. Automatic attack disruption stops active, fast-moving attacks such as ransomware campaigns by containing assets the moment the attack is recognized, with high confidence. All automatic actions can be undone. Contain device. Defender for Endpoint (blocks traffic to and from the device). Contain I P for undiscovered devices. Defender for Endpoint. Contain user. Defender for Endpoint (enforced at the endpoint; also used by predictive shielding). Isolate device. Defender for Endpoint (automatic isolation is in preview). Disable user. Defender for Identity (cloud-only accounts through the managed app Microsoft Defender for Identity).

1.title: Automatic attack disruption, continued
1.text: Automatic attack disruption. Revoke user session, suspend user. Microsoft Entra I D. oh auth app compromise. Defender for Cloud Apps. Safeboot hardening, G P O hardening, proactive user containment. Predictive shielding. Okta and A W S disruption (through Sentinel) is in preview. Exam tip: Attack disruption contains; it does not clean up. After containment the analyst investigates and undoes the actions when needed.

1.title: Prerequisites
1.text: Prerequisites. License. Microsoft three sixty-five E five or A five or Defender for Endpoint Plan two among other qualifying products. Device discovery. Standard discovery (needed for contain device). Device group. The automation level must not be No automated response. Contain user. Sense agent version ten point eight four seven zero or later. Defender for Identity. Auditing on domain controllers; action accounts (default Local System). Defender for Cloud Apps. Microsoft three sixty-five connector with all boxes selected, including Microsoft Entra I D apps. Defender for Office three sixty-five. Mailboxes in Exchange Online; audit events Mail Items Accessed, Update Inbox Rules, Move To Deleted Items, Soft Delete, Hard Delete. Turn it on in Settings, then Endpoints, then General, then Advanced features, then Configure automatic attack disruption. Roles that can configure it include Global Administrator, Security Administrator and Security Operator.

1.title: Seeing what disruption did
1.text: Seeing what disruption did. Incident queue. The tag Attack Disruption. Incident page. A yellow banner. Activities tab. A Policy status column. Action center. An entry for each action, with undo. Advanced hunting. Table Disruption And Response Events (preview).

1.title: Exclusions
1.text: Exclusions. Path: Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then Automated response. Identities. Add user exclusion (for example a break-glass account). Devices, then Device groups. Set the automation level per group; excluding a group also affects A I R. Devices, then Policy application. Create rule against a tag; Exclude I P.

1.title: Exclusions, continued
1.text: Exclusions. Permissions: with unified R back off, Security Administrator or Global Administrator; with it on, Security Operator or Core security settings (manage). A full opt-out needs a support case titled Attack disruption opt-out; Microsoft does not recommend it. Exam tip: Exclude a break-glass or critical service account with a user exclusion, not by turning the feature off for everyone.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Automatic attack disruption contained a device and disabled a user during a suspected ransomware attack. The analyst finds a false positive. What is the right next step? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Review the Action center and undo the containment actions. Every automatic attack disruption action can be undone from the Action center.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A break-glass administrator account must never be disabled by automatic attack disruption. What should be configured? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A user exclusion under Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then Automated response. The Identities tab of Automated response has Add user exclusion.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A device group is set to No automated response. What is the effect on automatic attack disruption for the devices in that group? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Containment is not applied because the prerequisite is not met. The device group automation level must not be No automated response.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An analyst filters the incident queue for incidents where Microsoft acted automatically to contain an attack. Which tag should the analyst look for? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Attack Disruption, which marks contained attacks. Incidents where attack disruption acted carry the Attack Disruption tag.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Fifty pending file quarantine actions of the same type are waiting. The analyst wants to approve them quickly. What should the analyst do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Multi-select the actions of the same type in Action center, then Pending. The Pending tab supports multi-select for actions of the same type.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Automatic attack disruption must disable a cloud-only user account. Which component performs the action? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The managed enterprise app named Microsoft Defender for Identity. Cloud-only accounts are disabled through the Microsoft-managed enterprise app Microsoft Defender for Identity.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the three A I R verdicts? Answer: Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found. Question two. Where are pending remediation actions approved? Answer: Action center, then Pending. Question three. Which device discovery mode does contain device need? Answer: Standard discovery.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which minimum sense agent version does contain user need? Answer: ten point eight four seven zero. Question five. Where are attack disruption exclusions configured? Answer: Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then Automated response. Question six. Which hunting table records disruption events? Answer: Disruption And Response Events (preview).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. A I R: verdicts Malicious, Suspicious, No threats found; approve in Action center, then Pending. Change: since September one, twenty twenty-six no separate A I R experience for Defender for Endpoint alerts. Disruption actions: contain device, contain I P, contain user, isolate, disable user, revoke session, oh auth app. Prerequisites: E five or Plan two, standard discovery, automation level not No automated response. Visibility: tag Attack Disruption, yellow banner, Action center, Disruption And Response Events. Exclusions: Settings, then Microsoft Defender X D R, then Automated response.
